title: Why Billionaires Pay So Little Tax

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是 Benjamin Poulin，我是 Mark Ronson，欢迎收听《The Reframers》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店打碟的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着 300 件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《The Reframers》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的 Michael Barbaro。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《The Daily》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: An explosive news story shedding light on the taxes paid by the ultra-wealthy.
sentences.zh: 一则重磅新闻，揭露了超级富豪们缴纳的税款情况。

sentences.en: They're the biggest billionaires in America behind brands like Amazon and Tesla.
sentences.zh: 他们是美国最大的亿万富翁，背后是亚马逊和特斯拉这样的品牌。

sentences.en: They're paying little in income taxes compared to their fortunes, sometimes nothing at all.
sentences.zh: 与他们的巨额财富相比，他们缴纳的所得税微乎其微，有时甚至一分钱都不交。

sentences.en: Secret documents obtained by ProPublica from inside the IRS.
sentences.zh: ProPublica 从美国国税局（IRS）内部获得的机密文件显示，

sentences.en: Newsflash, John, the super rich, they're not like us.
sentences.zh: 新闻快讯，John，超级富豪们和我们不一样。

sentences.en: Are reigniting a long-simmering debate about why the ultra-wealthy are taxed so differently than those who earn far less.
sentences.zh: 这重新引发了一场长期存在的争论：为什么超级富豪的纳税方式与普通工薪阶层如此不同。

sentences.en: Now the scandal is what they're doing is perfectly legal.
sentences.zh: 现在的丑闻在于，他们的做法完全合法。

sentences.en: Sabrina Tavernisi spoke with our colleague, Jonathan Weissman, about how that came to be and what it would take to change it.
sentences.zh: Sabrina Tavernisi 与我们的同事 Jonathan Weissman 探讨了这种情况是如何形成的，以及需要做出什么改变。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, June 15th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 6 月 15 日，星期二。

sentences.en: Okay, Jonathan, talk me through exactly what we learned from this report last week.
sentences.zh: 好的，Jonathan，请详细说明一下我们上周从这份报告中了解到了什么。

sentences.en: It was a shocker because what we saw were household names.
sentences.zh: 这令人震惊，因为我们看到的全是家喻户晓的名字。

sentences.en: People like Jeff Bezos, Michael Bloomberg, Elon Musk, George Soros paid virtually nothing in taxes.
sentences.zh: 像杰夫·贝佐斯、迈克尔·布隆伯格、埃隆·马斯克、乔治·索罗斯这样的人，几乎没交什么税。

sentences.en: And in some years, they paid zero taxes.
sentences.zh: 有些年份，他们缴纳的税款为零。

sentences.en: And what is remarkable is that they weren't breaking the law.
sentences.zh: 最引人注目的是，他们并没有触犯法律。

sentences.en: They were using the tax code as Congress wrote it and as the Internal Revenue Service interpreted it.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在利用国会制定的税法以及国税局的解读方式。

sentences.en: Everything they did was perfectly legal.
sentences.zh: 他们所做的一切完全合法。

sentences.en: How is that possible?
sentences.zh: 这怎么可能呢？

sentences.en: Well, Jeff Bezos is not like you and I.
sentences.zh: 嗯，杰夫·贝佐斯和你我不同。

sentences.en: Hey, he doesn't make his money the way we do.
sentences.zh: 嘿，他的赚钱方式和我们不一样。

sentences.en: Let's take a firefighter.
sentences.zh: 我们以消防员为例。

sentences.en: A firefighter maybe makes $40,000, $50,000 a year.
sentences.zh: 消防员一年的收入可能在 4 万到 5 万美元左右。

sentences.en: And all of that money is coming in the form of a paycheck.
sentences.zh: 所有的钱都是以工资的形式发放的。

sentences.en: And before that paycheck even lands in the firefighter's bank account, the federal government and the state government has already extracted its taxes.
sentences.zh: 在工资进入消防员银行账户之前，联邦政府和州政府就已经扣除了税款。

sentences.en: He's been taxed on his income.
sentences.zh: 他已经为自己的收入纳了税。

sentences.en: And that firefighter's tax rate should be about 22% according to the current tax code.
sentences.zh: 根据现行税法，这位消防员的税率应该在 22% 左右。

sentences.en: Bezos also has an income.
sentences.zh: 贝佐斯也有收入。

sentences.en: His salary is $81,840 a year.
sentences.zh: 他的年薪是 81,840 美元。

sentences.en: Pretty modeSt.
sentences.zh: 相当谦虚。

sentences.en: Okay, that is very, very low number for the CEO of Amazon.
sentences.zh: 好的，对于亚马逊的首席执行官来说，这个数字非常非常低。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's on purpose, right?
sentences.zh: 而且这是故意的，对吧？

sentences.en: So, Jonathan, obviously Bezos' real income is a lot bigger than $81,000.
sentences.zh: 所以，Jonathan，显然贝佐斯的实际收入远不止 8 万美元。

sentences.en: So where does his income come from if it's not a paycheck?
sentences.zh: 如果不是工资，那他的收入从哪里来？

sentences.en: And what does that have to do with how he gets taxed?
sentences.zh: 这和他如何纳税有什么关系？

sentences.en: So Jeff Bezos' vast, vast fortune, most of that is in assets.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·贝佐斯拥有极其庞大的财富，其中大部分是资产。

sentences.en: And most of those assets are stocks.
sentences.zh: 而这些资产大部分是股票。

sentences.en: Remember, when he first started Amazon, he would have gotten a lot of stocks right up front.
sentences.zh: 记住，当他刚创办亚马逊时，他一开始就获得了大量股票。

sentences.en: And those stocks are part of his pay.
sentences.zh: 这些股票是他薪酬的一部分。

sentences.en: You know, he is given certain stock options every year.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他每年都会获得一定的股票期权。

sentences.en: So those stocks accumulate worth as the value of Amazon rises and the stock market rises.
sentences.zh: 随着亚马逊价值的提升和股市的上涨，这些股票的价值也在不断累积。

sentences.en: And they're just sitting there gaining wealth, getting fatter, more expensive.
sentences.zh: 它们就放在那里增值，变得越来越丰厚、越来越昂贵。

sentences.en: Now, for ordinary wealthy people, for the merely wealthy, people like doctors or lawyers, they also have a lot of money in stocks.
sentences.zh: 对于普通的富人，也就是仅仅是有钱的人，比如医生或律师，他们也有很多钱在股票里。

sentences.en: And when they need a big chunk of change, let's say they want to go buy a car or put down money for a house.
sentences.zh: 当他们需要一大笔钱时，比如想买车或付房子的首付，

sentences.en: They need to go into those stocks, those assets, and sell a big chunk of them.
sentences.zh: 他们就需要动用这些股票和资产，卖掉很大一部分。

sentences.en: And when they sell, they actually do pay a tax.
sentences.zh: 而当他们出售时，他们确实需要纳税。

sentences.en: It is called the capital gains tax.
sentences.zh: 这被称为资本利得税。

sentences.en: Right now, the capital gains tax is less than an income tax for most people.
sentences.zh: 目前，对大多数人来说，资本利得税低于所得税。

sentences.en: For a really, really rich person, it's about 20%.
sentences.zh: 对于真正非常有钱的人来说，税率大约是 20%。

sentences.en: So let's say you bought a stock for $20.
sentences.zh: 假设你以 20 美元买入一只股票。

sentences.en: You sold it for $30.
sentences.zh: 你以 30 美元卖出。

sentences.en: You have to pay tax on the $10 gain.
sentences.zh: 你必须为 10 美元的收益纳税。

sentences.en: So you'd pay $2 if your tax bracket is 20% of capital gains.
sentences.zh: 如果你的资本利得税率是 20%，那么你需要支付 2 美元。

sentences.en: Now, Bezos is different because he has so much money,
sentences.zh: 贝佐斯的情况不同，因为他太有钱了，

sentences.en: he doesn't have to sell anything to come up with a big chunk of change that he might need to purchase something like his eighth house.
sentences.zh: 他不需要卖掉任何东西就能凑出他购买第八套房子所需的大笔资金。

sentences.en: And that's why the ProPublica article was so interesting, because we learned from that how he can be buying all the things we see him buying and still paying zero in taxes.
sentences.zh: 这就是 ProPublica 那篇文章如此有趣的原因，因为我们从中了解到他如何能在购买我们所见的一切的同时，依然缴纳零税款。

sentences.en: Okay, so why don't you walk me through that?
sentences.zh: 好的，那你能不能给我解释一下？

sentences.en: How is Bezos actually doing it?
sentences.zh: 贝佐斯到底是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: So let's say Jeff Bezos needs $100 million to buy his next big house.
sentences.zh: 假设杰夫·贝佐斯需要 1 亿美元来买下一套豪宅。

sentences.en: You know, he could easily sell $100 million in stocks or bonds to come up with that, but he doesn't want to pay taxes on the sale of any of those assets.
sentences.zh: 他可以轻松卖掉 1 亿美元的股票或债券来凑钱，但他不想为出售这些资产缴纳税款。

sentences.en: So what a Jeff Bezos gets to do is go down to his bank and say, hey, you know me, I'm good for this money.
sentences.zh: 所以杰夫·贝佐斯可以去银行说，嘿，你了解我，我有偿还能力。

sentences.en: Could you give me a low-interest $100 million loan?
sentences.zh: 你能给我一笔 1 亿美元的低息贷款吗？

sentences.en: I have the collateral.
sentences.zh: 我有抵押品。

sentences.en: Here it is.
sentences.zh: 就在这里。

sentences.en: Give me $100 million.
sentences.zh: 给我 1 亿美元。

sentences.en: And the banks are perfectly happy to give Jeff Bezos $100 million, no problem.
sentences.zh: 银行非常乐意给杰夫·贝佐斯 1 亿美元，没问题。

sentences.en: And not only do you not have to pay a tax because you didn't sell anything to get that $100 million, you actually get to write some of that loan off your taxes.
sentences.zh: 而且你不仅不需要纳税，因为你没有卖掉任何东西来获得这 1 亿美元，你甚至还可以将部分贷款从税款中抵扣。

sentences.en: That's the way the tax code works.
sentences.zh: 这就是税法的运作方式。

sentences.en: Okay, so let me get this straight.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我理清一下。

sentences.en: So when Bezos wants to buy something expensive, he doesn't just sell some stocks.
sentences.zh: 所以当贝佐斯想买昂贵的东西时，他不会直接卖掉股票。

sentences.en: He takes out a loan backed by all of his rising assets, his enormous wealth, and banks happily give it to him because they know he's good for it.
sentences.zh: 他会以不断升值的资产和巨额财富作为抵押进行贷款，银行也很乐意借给他，因为他们知道他有偿还能力。

sentences.en: And that's his spending money.
sentences.zh: 这就是他的消费资金。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That seems like a pretty big loophole in the tax system.
sentences.zh: 这看起来像是税收体系中一个很大的漏洞。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: And not only by not selling is he avoiding capital gains tax on the sale, he also gets to keep his assets intact.
sentences.zh: 而且他不仅通过不卖出资产避免了资本利得税，还保持了资产的完整性。

sentences.en: And those assets keep growing in value over a year, over a year, over a year.
sentences.zh: 这些资产年复一年地不断增值。

sentences.en: And his wealth grows and grows and grows and is never taxed as long as he doesn't sell it.
sentences.zh: 他的财富不断增长，只要他不卖出，就永远不用纳税。

sentences.en: Under the U.S.
sentences.zh: 根据美国

sentences.en: tax code, you only pay taxes when you sell something.
sentences.zh: 税法，你只有在卖出东西时才需要纳税。

sentences.en: So just don't sell anything.
sentences.zh: 所以只要不卖就行了。

sentences.en: But he does have to pay off that loan, right, for his $100 million house.
sentences.zh: 但他必须偿还那笔贷款，对吧，为了他那 1 亿美元的房子。

sentences.en: So how does he get the money to do that?
sentences.zh: 那他从哪里弄钱来还呢？

sentences.en: Does he have to liquidate some assets to do that?
sentences.zh: 他必须变卖一些资产吗？

sentences.en: And then wouldn't he need to pay taxes on whatever money he gets from that?
sentences.zh: 那样的话，他难道不需要为获得的钱纳税吗？

sentences.en: Remember, he does have some income coming in.
sentences.zh: 记住，他确实有一些收入来源。

sentences.en: He's got that $81,000 salary.
sentences.zh: 他有那 8.1 万美元的薪水。

sentences.en: So he can pay off, you know, on monthly installments, some of these loans.
sentences.zh: 所以他可以按月分期偿还部分贷款。

sentences.en: The other thing he does, which is what a lot of rich people do, is you take out loans to pay loans.
sentences.zh: 他做的另一件事，也是许多富人所做的，就是借新债还旧债。

sentences.en: So you keep rolling over debt.
sentences.zh: 所以你一直在滚动债务。

sentences.en: So let's say your big loan bill comes due.
sentences.zh: 假设你的大额贷款到期了。

sentences.en: You go to a different bank and say, can I take another loan out?
sentences.zh: 你去另一家银行说，我能再贷一笔款吗？

sentences.en: And in fact, every time you do that, you're actually decreasing your tax burden that much more.
sentences.zh: 事实上，每次你这样做，你实际上都在进一步减轻你的税负。

sentences.en: Because all of these lending transactions are, many of them are tax deductible.
sentences.zh: 因为所有这些借贷交易中，有很多是可以抵税的。

sentences.en: So is Bezos in an immense amount of debt?
sentences.zh: 所以贝佐斯背负着巨额债务吗？

sentences.en: Now, we don't really have a perfect picture of his balance sheet.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有他资产负债表的完整情况。

sentences.en: But he probably holds a lot of debt.
sentences.zh: 但他可能持有大量债务。

sentences.en: Because rich people tend to hold a lot of debt.
sentences.zh: 因为富人往往持有大量债务。

sentences.en: It's actually part of tax management.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是税务管理的一部分。

sentences.en: And I wouldn't be surprised if his debt is, by human standards, probably fairly large.
sentences.zh: 如果他的债务以人类标准来看相当大，我一点也不会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: But by Jeff Bezos' standards, against his assets, against what he's worth, it's still probably a small sum.
sentences.zh: 但以杰夫·贝佐斯的标准来看，相对于他的资产和身价，这可能仍然是一笔小数目。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But how common is this?
sentences.zh: 但这有多普遍？

sentences.en: I mean, is your average wealthy finance guy doing this?
sentences.zh: 我是说，普通的富人金融从业者也在这样做吗？

sentences.en: Or is this just Jeff Bezos?
sentences.zh: 还是这只是杰夫·贝佐斯个人的做法？

sentences.en: I think it really applies to the really mega rich.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实适用于超级富豪。

sentences.en: A doctor might be worth tens of millions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 一位医生可能拥有数千万美元的资产。

sentences.en: But for that doctor, a lot of these transactions would be quite expensive.
sentences.zh: 但对于那位医生来说，很多这样的交易成本会非常高。

sentences.en: You know, every time you go down to the bank, it's not free.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每次你去银行都不是免费的。

sentences.en: And you're also paying lawyers who really know how to do this.
sentences.zh: 而且你还要支付那些真正懂得如何操作的律师费用。

sentences.en: Now, that legal bill for Jeff Bezos is nothing.
sentences.zh: 对于杰夫·贝佐斯来说，那点律师费根本不算什么。

sentences.en: But that legal bill for a doctor would be probably prohibitive.
sentences.zh: 但对于医生来说，这笔律师费可能是无法承受的。

sentences.en: And I don't think you see this as widely as one might think.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这种情况像人们想象的那么普遍。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So for Bezos, he's thinking to himself, okay, I need all this money to live.
sentences.zh: 所以对贝佐斯来说，他心想，好吧，我需要这些钱来生活。

sentences.en: I can either pay myself a big salary from Amazon, my company, and pay income taxes on that.
sentences.zh: 我可以从我的公司亚马逊给自己发高薪，并为此缴纳所得税。

sentences.en: Or I can sell off a bunch of stock that I own and pay capital gains taxes on that.
sentences.zh: 或者我可以卖掉我拥有的一堆股票，并为此缴纳资本利得税。

sentences.en: Or I can ask a bank to give me the money untaxed based on the fact that I have all of these growing assets.
sentences.zh: 或者我可以要求银行基于我拥有这些不断增值的资产，给我一笔免税的资金。

sentences.en: Kind of a no-brainer.
sentences.zh: 这简直是不言而喻的选择。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这就是美国

sentences.en: tax code.
sentences.zh: 税法。

sentences.en: And it goes way back.
sentences.zh: 而且由来已久。

sentences.en: There is a long history,
sentences.zh: 有着悠久的历史，

sentences.en: year after year, law after law, that has created a tax system that lets the super rich off the hook while you and I pay our taxes week in, week out,
sentences.zh: 年复一年，法律一条接一条，创造了一个让超级富豪逃避纳税的税收体系，而你我却要每周从工资中缴纳税款。

sentences.en: out of our paycheck.
sentences.zh: 从我们的工资中扣除。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是 Andrew Ross-Sorkin。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日，我将在纽约市的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: Vance、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、Zylran Mondani 等人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无保留、未经修饰的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在 11 月 18 日在 NYTimes.com 上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，阅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Okay, Jonathan, where does that long history of letting the super rich off the hook start?
sentences.zh: 好的，Jonathan，这种让超级富豪逃税的悠久历史是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: Well, to understand how we got to Jeff Bezos paying no income tax at all some years,
sentences.zh: 嗯，要理解我们是如何走到杰夫·贝佐斯某些年份完全不缴纳所得税这一步的，

sentences.en: you have to understand how taxation of investment broke off from the taxation of income and paychecks.
sentences.zh: 你必须了解投资税收是如何从所得税和工资税中分离出来的。

sentences.en: And to do that, you really have to go back to the beginning of the federal income tax in 1913.
sentences.zh: 要做到这一点，你必须回到 1913 年联邦所得税的开端。

sentences.en: And from the very beginning, the United States was not afraid to soak the rich.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，美国就不怕向富人征税。

sentences.en: That first income tax included a 6% surtax on incomes over $500,000.
sentences.zh: 最初的所得税包括对超过 50 万美元的收入征收 6% 的附加税。

sentences.en: I mean, that is a very high tax rate on rich people, considering today the highest income tax rate is 37%.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，考虑到今天最高的所得税率是 37%，这对富人来说是一个非常高的税率。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I'm thinking of Vanderbilt's, Carnegie's, Rockefeller.
sentences.zh: 我在想范德比尔特、卡内基、洛克菲勒这些人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And those guys were traditional moneymakers, right?
sentences.zh: 这些人是传统的赚钱大亨，对吧？

sentences.en: They had companies that made things.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有制造实体的公司。

sentences.en: So the Vanderbilt's and the Rockefeller's, they sold oil, they sold steel, and the sales of those things came back to them as income.
sentences.zh: 所以范德比尔特和洛克菲勒他们卖石油、卖钢铁，这些销售额最终都变成了他们的收入。

sentences.en: And that income was taxed at very high rates at the highest levels.
sentences.zh: 而这些收入在最高层级上被征收了非常高的税率。

sentences.en: That's amazing in today's context.
sentences.zh: 在今天看来，这简直不可思议。

sentences.en: I mean, did everybody basically agree that that made sense to tax the wealthy at a much higher rate?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当时大家基本上都认同对富人征收高得多的税是合理的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, they basically did.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们基本上都认同。

sentences.en: You know, the United States had a different attitude towards the rich than they do today.
sentences.zh: 你要知道，美国当时对富人的态度与今天截然不同。

sentences.en: Remember, we called them robber barons.
sentences.zh: 别忘了，我们曾称他们为“强盗男爵”。

sentences.en: We had a president, Teddy Roosevelt, who campaigned on trust busting.
sentences.zh: 我们有一位总统，西奥多·罗斯福，他竞选时的口号就是反托拉斯。

sentences.en: It was politically popular to go after the rich.
sentences.zh: 打击富人在当时是深得民心的政治举措。

sentences.en: You know, in 1944, during World War II, the highest marginal tax rate was 91%.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在1944年二战期间，最高边际税率曾高达91%。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in fact, when John Kennedy came in, he talked about a rising tide lifting all boats and that we need to do something to encourage wealth.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当约翰·肯尼迪上台时，他谈到了“潮涨船高”，并表示我们需要采取措施来鼓励财富增长。

sentences.en: Well, you know what he did?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道他做了什么吗？

sentences.en: He said he cut the highest tax rate from 92% to 77%.
sentences.zh: 他说他把最高税率从92%降到了77%。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: That is still extremely high by today's standards.
sentences.zh: 以今天的标准来看，这依然高得离谱。

sentences.en: Extremely.
sentences.zh: 非常高。

sentences.en: And it stayed that way, basically, until Ronald Reagan.
sentences.zh: 而且这种情况基本一直持续到了罗纳德·里根时期。

sentences.en: I'd like to say a few words about where this country's been and where we'll be going from here.
sentences.zh: 我想就这个国家过去的发展历程以及未来的走向说几句。

sentences.en: The last time I visited the New York Stock Exchange was in 1980, and the mood sure was different then.
sentences.zh: 我上一次访问纽约证券交易所是在1980年，那时的氛围确实与现在不同。

sentences.en: But in the last five years, we've moved from malaise to hope, confidence, and opportunity.
sentences.zh: 但在过去五年里，我们已经从低迷走向了希望、信心和机遇。

sentences.en: So, you know, Ronald Reagan comes in at a time when the Cold War is raging.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，罗纳德·里根上台时正值冷战激烈之时。

sentences.en: It's the go-go 80s.
sentences.zh: 那是充满活力的80年代。

sentences.en: We're bullish on the American economy.
sentences.zh: 我们看好美国经济。

sentences.en: This is the trading floor of the New York Stock Exchange, the nerve center of American capitalism.
sentences.zh: 这里是纽约证券交易所的交易大厅，是美国资本主义的中枢神经。

sentences.en: Finance is king.
sentences.zh: 金融为王。

sentences.en: The point is, ladies and gentlemen, that greed is good.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，重点是，贪婪是好事。

sentences.en: Gordon Gekko is proclaiming that greed is good.
sentences.zh: 戈登·盖柯宣称贪婪是好事。

sentences.en: The Dow Jones closing index went from 759 to a high of 2791.
sentences.zh: 道琼斯收盘指数从759点一路飙升至2791点的高位。

sentences.en: The image of the rich has changed.
sentences.zh: 富人的形象已经改变了。

sentences.en: Business news and business schools were in.
sentences.zh: 商业新闻和商学院成了热门。

sentences.en: The NBA was the degree of the decade.
sentences.zh: MBA成了那个年代的标配学位。

sentences.en: CEOs and corporate raiders became celebrities.
sentences.zh: 首席执行官和企业狙击手成了名人。

sentences.en: And there was a point where Ronald Reagan is trying to reform the tax code.
sentences.zh: 当时罗纳德·里根正试图改革税法。

sentences.en: And he's talking to Bill Bradley, the senator from New Jersey, who had been a professional basketball player.
sentences.zh: 他与来自新泽西州的参议员比尔·布拉德利交谈，后者曾是一名职业篮球运动员。

sentences.en: And Reagan tells Bradley, you know, the income tax is so high, I didn't want to make another movie.
sentences.zh: 里根告诉布拉德利，你知道，所得税太高了，我都不想再拍电影了。

sentences.en: It didn't make any sense economically to make another movie.
sentences.zh: 从经济角度来看，再拍一部电影根本没意义。

sentences.en: And Bradley says, yeah, you know, I didn't want to play for the NBA anymore.
sentences.zh: 布拉德利说，是啊，我也不想再为NBA打球了。

sentences.en: What's the point?
sentences.zh: 有什么意义呢？

sentences.en: I was just going to be taxed away.
sentences.zh: 反正赚的钱都要被税收走。

sentences.en: And they come up with a 1986 tax reform that lowers the highest income tax rate all the way down to 28%.
sentences.zh: 于是他们推出了1986年的税制改革，将最高所得税率一路降至28%。

sentences.en: I feel like we've just played the world series of tax reform and the American people won.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们刚刚打赢了税改的世界大赛，而美国人民赢了。

sentences.en: Virtually a century of soaking the rich goes down to the rich paying not a whole lot more in income tax than anyone else.
sentences.zh: 近一个世纪以来“劫富”的传统，最终变成了富人在所得税上交的钱并不比其他人多多少。

sentences.en: So instead of this pervasive feeling that the rich should be taxed and should be taxed heavily to pay for things the government needs,
sentences.zh: 所以，那种认为富人应该被征税，而且应该被重税以支付政府所需开支的普遍观念，

sentences.en: now it's shifted to rich guys are actually good for the country and for the economy.
sentences.zh: 现在已经转变为富人实际上对国家和经济有益。

sentences.en: And they shouldn't be punished with a bunch of taxes because, after all, we're Americans.
sentences.zh: 而且他们不应该受到一堆税收的惩罚，毕竟，我们是美国人。

sentences.en: This is our capitalist spirit.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的资本主义精神。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So by the 1990s, the economy is really transforming.
sentences.zh: 所以到了90年代，经济正在发生真正的转型。

sentences.en: America makes its money off money.
sentences.zh: 美国靠钱生钱。

sentences.en: Finance is spinning off all sorts of wealth.
sentences.zh: 金融业正在衍生出各种各样的财富。

sentences.en: The stock market begins to boom.
sentences.zh: 股市开始繁荣。

sentences.en: There are day traders.
sentences.zh: 出现了日内交易员。

sentences.en: And we had the beginning of the internet.
sentences.zh: 我们还迎来了互联网的开端。

sentences.en: The economy is turning into something completely different.
sentences.zh: 经济正在变成完全不同的东西。

sentences.en: And it's being driven by investment and risk.
sentences.zh: 它正由投资和风险驱动。

sentences.en: OK, so it's no longer rich people like the Vandervelts making things.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以不再是像范德比尔特那样制造实体的富人了。

sentences.en: It's people involved in finance on a mass scale.
sentences.zh: 而是大规模参与金融的人。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Remember, along comes Newt Gingrich and the Republican Revolution of 1994.
sentences.zh: 别忘了，纽特·金里奇和1994年的共和党革命随之而来。

sentences.en: We're here because we are taking the first steps.
sentences.zh: 我们来到这里，是因为我们正在迈出第一步。

sentences.en: And we're taking them in a contract with the American people.
sentences.zh: 我们正在履行与美国人民的契约。

sentences.en: And Gingrich begins a mantra that we need to treat income from investment differently from income from work.
sentences.zh: 金里奇开始宣扬一种理念，即我们需要区别对待投资收入和劳动收入。

sentences.en: We want to make sure that people who create jobs by saving and by investing have a tax break to increase economic growth.
sentences.zh: 我们要确保那些通过储蓄和投资创造就业机会的人能获得税收减免，以促进经济增长。

sentences.en: And I think there's a broad agreement now on that.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在对此已经达成了广泛共识。

sentences.en: That, in fact, we need to favor income from investment.
sentences.zh: 即事实上，我们需要优待投资收入。

sentences.en: You know, as Gingrich was actually trying to balance the budget with Bill Clinton, he said, We favor abolishing the tax on savings and job creation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当金里奇试图与比尔·克林顿平衡预算时，他说：“我们主张废除储蓄和创造就业的税收。”

sentences.en: We favor...
sentences.zh: 我们主张……

sentences.en: I favor zero tax on savings and job creation.
sentences.zh: 我主张对储蓄和创造就业实行零税收。

sentences.en: That was 1997, which meant he didn't want to tax investment income at all.
sentences.zh: 那是1997年，这意味着他根本不想对投资收入征税。

sentences.en: Explain the idea behind that.
sentences.zh: 解释一下这背后的想法。

sentences.en: Why would Gingrich say something like that?
sentences.zh: 为什么金里奇会说那样的话？

sentences.en: Because, well, first of all, of course, he did have a lot of rich benefactors.
sentences.zh: 因为，首先，他当然有很多富有的赞助人。

sentences.en: But there was a sense that if people invest money in the stock market, if they're giving companies their money, those companies would use it to innovate, to make new companies,
sentences.zh: 但当时有一种感觉，如果人们把钱投进股市，如果他们把钱交给公司，这些公司就会利用这些钱去创新，去创建新公司，

sentences.en: to find new products, to find new services.
sentences.zh: 去寻找新产品，去提供新服务。

sentences.en: And that would grow the economy as well.
sentences.zh: 这也会促进经济增长。

sentences.en: Well, there was an idea that we don't want people to just sit on their money.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当时有一种想法是，我们不希望人们只是守着钱不动。

sentences.en: We want them to invest it.
sentences.zh: 我们希望他们去投资。

sentences.en: We love the stock market.
sentences.zh: 我们热爱股市。

sentences.en: And in order to do that, we don't want to tax the gains that they're seeing the same way we tax the money coming from their paycheck.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，我们不想对他们看到的收益征收与工资收入相同的税。

sentences.en: We want to favor investment.
sentences.zh: 我们想要优待投资。

sentences.en: And this gave rise to a push for special treatments of capital gains taxes, those taxes that you pay off of the sale of stocks mainly, but also other assets.
sentences.zh: 这引发了对资本利得税进行特殊处理的呼声，这些税主要是针对股票销售，也包括其他资产。

sentences.en: So, Jonathan, was that the moment that was really the beginning of this thing we've been talking about, which is effectively the separation of investment and income?
sentences.zh: 那么，乔纳森，那是否就是我们一直在谈论的这件事的真正开端，即投资与收入的有效分离？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, at this point, investment income is considered better than regular income.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在这一点上，投资收入被认为比普通收入更好。

sentences.en: It's taxed at a lower rate.
sentences.zh: 它的税率更低。

sentences.en: The people with the most investments, the rich, are raking in money off the stock market.
sentences.zh: 拥有最多投资的人，也就是富人，正在从股市中大把捞钱。

sentences.en: It's not being taxed very heavily.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有被征收很重的税。

sentences.en: They're getting richer and richer and richer.
sentences.zh: 他们变得越来越富有。

sentences.en: The gap between rich and poor is getting wider and wider until it's a chasm.
sentences.zh: 贫富差距越来越大，直到变成一道鸿沟。

sentences.en: Democrats are arguing over capital gains rates that keep going up or down or up and down, considering whatever the political winds are.
sentences.zh: 民主党人正在争论资本利得税率是该上调还是下调，或者随着政治风向反复波动。

sentences.en: And meantime, nobody is talking about how to tax this growing wealth, how to capture the value of these huge piles of assets.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，没有人谈论如何对这些不断增长的财富征税，如何获取这些巨额资产的价值。

sentences.en: Nobody is talking about what the ProPublica article was talking about.
sentences.zh: 没有人谈论ProPublica那篇文章所讨论的内容。

sentences.en: That is, nobody until Elizabeth Warren in 2019.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，在2019年伊丽莎白·沃伦提出之前，没人谈论。

sentences.en: It's time for a wealth tax in America.
sentences.zh: 是时候在美国征收财富税了。

sentences.en: Elizabeth Warren says we need to rethink the way we tax in America and we need to begin taxing wealth.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·沃伦说，我们需要重新思考美国的税收方式，我们需要开始对财富征税。

sentences.en: Your first $50 million is free and clear.
sentences.zh: 你的前5000万美元是免税的。

sentences.en: I see some folks going, phew, okay.
sentences.zh: 我看到有些人松了一口气，心想，呼，好吧。

sentences.en: But your 50 millionth and first dollar, you got to pitch in two cents.
sentences.zh: 但超过5000万的那部分，你得贡献两美分。

sentences.en: And her plan has been through a bunch of iterations, but essentially it comes down to something like this.
sentences.zh: 她的计划经过了多次迭代，但本质上归结为这样一种方案。

sentences.en: If you're worth at least $50 million, you need to pay a 2% surtax on the value of your wealth above that threshold each year, whether you sold any of it or not.
sentences.zh: 如果你拥有至少5000万美元的资产，你每年需要对超过该门槛的财富价值缴纳2%的附加税，无论你是否卖出过任何资产。

sentences.en: You've been paying a wealth tax forever.
sentences.zh: 你们一直都在缴纳财富税。

sentences.en: They just call it a property tax.
sentences.zh: 他们只是把它称为房产税。

sentences.en: I'm just saying for the bazillionaires, the top one-tenth of one percent,
sentences.zh: 我只是说对于那些亿万富翁，也就是那前0.1%的人，

sentences.en: how about we include, in addition to the real estate, the stock portfolio, the diamonds, the Rembrandts, and the yachts?
sentences.zh: 除了房地产，我们把股票投资组合、钻石、伦勃朗画作和游艇也算进去怎么样？

sentences.en: That's all.
sentences.zh: 就这些。

sentences.en: Now, her plan would start with stocks, but eventually it would encompass all kinds of wealth taxed at 2% above that $50 million threshold.
sentences.zh: 现在，她的计划将从股票开始，但最终将涵盖所有类型的财富，对超过5000万美元门槛的部分征收2%的税。

sentences.en: And then there'd be an additional 1% tax on wealth above a billion dollars.
sentences.zh: 然后对超过10亿美元的财富再额外征收1%的税。

sentences.en: I mean, we all do, in some ways, pay taxes on our assets because we pay property taxes, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某种程度上，我们都在为我们的资产纳税，因为我们缴纳房产税，对吧？

sentences.en: Every year, somebody comes around from my city and tells me my house has gained a certain amount of value and my property tax goes up some amount because of that rise in value.
sentences.zh: 每年，我所在的城市都会有人来告诉我，我的房子增值了多少，我的房产税也因为这种增值而上涨了一些。

sentences.en: That's what she's saying we should do for everything.
sentences.zh: 这就是她所说的我们应该对所有事物采取的做法。

sentences.en: So when she proposes this, that's kind of a radically new way of thinking about what we tax in our country.
sentences.zh: 所以当她提出这一点时，这在某种程度上是一种关于我们国家应该对什么征税的激进新思维。

sentences.en: But clearly it wasn't persuasive enough because we don't have a wealth tax now, right?
sentences.zh: 但显然它不够有说服力，因为我们现在还没有财富税，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, you're right.
sentences.zh: 是的，你是对的。

sentences.en: It did not have the political firepower to win her the nomination for the presidency, and it has not gotten through Congress.
sentences.zh: 它没有足够的政治火力让她赢得总统提名，也没有在国会通过。

sentences.en: But Democratic lawmakers that I've talked to in the last week, especially since that ProPublica article came out, are saying they really want to do this.
sentences.zh: 但我过去一周交谈过的民主党议员，特别是在那篇ProPublica文章发表后，都表示他们真的很想这样做。

sentences.en: The tax writing committees, the Finance Committee and the Ways and Means Committee, are tasked to pay for all of these things that Democrats, especially Joe Biden, want to do.
sentences.zh: 税收起草委员会，即财政委员会和筹款委员会，被委以重任，要为民主党人，特别是乔·拜登想要做的所有事情买单。

sentences.en: They want to spend a lot more money on infrastructure, they want universal pre-K, they want universal access to community colleges.
sentences.zh: 他们想在基础设施上投入更多资金，他们想要全民学前教育，他们想要全民普及社区大学。

sentences.en: All these things cost money.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都需要钱。

sentences.en: And while Republicans are trying to avoid raising taxes, Democrats suddenly see a real reason to do something about wealth, to tax wealth,
sentences.zh: 虽然共和党人试图避免增税，但民主党人突然看到了对财富采取行动、对财富征税的真正理由，

sentences.en: because they see it as a big political winner, especially now that we know that the richest of the rich don't pay taxes.
sentences.zh: 因为他们认为这是一个巨大的政治加分项，尤其是现在我们知道最富有的人并不纳税。

sentences.en: In your mind, is there any reason to think that this might actually happen?
sentences.zh: 在你看来，有什么理由认为这真的可能发生吗？

sentences.en: You know, I think it really might.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为真的有可能。

sentences.en: The biggest impediment to it happening might be, ironically, the Democratic desire to work with Republicans on a bipartisan bill,
sentences.zh: 实现这一目标的最大障碍，讽刺的是，可能是民主党人希望与共和党人合作达成两党法案的愿望，

sentences.en: because Republicans are never going to go along with anything like a wealth tax.
sentences.zh: 因为共和党人永远不会同意任何类似财富税的东西。

sentences.en: If the Democrats decide to forget about bipartisanship and pass, say, a grand infrastructure bill on their own, they'll use some kind of wealth tax to help pay for that.
sentences.zh: 如果民主党人决定放弃两党合作，自行通过一项大型基础设施法案，他们会利用某种财富税来帮助支付费用。

sentences.en: So in the end, partisanship is the thing that will push this issue forward.
sentences.zh: 所以最终，党派之争将是推动这一议题前进的动力。

sentences.en: Bipartisanship will be the thing that kills it.
sentences.zh: 而两党合作反而会成为扼杀它的因素。

sentences.en: Interesting, huh?
sentences.zh: 有意思吧？

sentences.en: I mean, if they can get Joe Manchin to vote for it, you know, they can do it with 50 votes in the Senate and they certainly will be able to get it through the House.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果他们能让乔·曼钦投票支持，你知道，他们可以在参议院以50票通过，而且他们肯定能让它在众议院通过。

sentences.en: So it's still a long shot, but it's not a pipe dream because they can do it with just Democratic votes as long as they have the presidency and both houses of Congress.
sentences.zh: 所以这仍然是一个渺茫的机会，但并非痴人说梦，因为只要他们拥有总统职位和国会两院，他们就可以仅凭民主党的选票做到这一点。

sentences.en: So this idea of a wealth tax, it's political, of course, but it's also, it seems to me,
sentences.zh: 所以这个财富税的想法，当然是政治性的，但它在我看来，

sentences.en: very foundational to how we think about wealth in this country and our economy and how our economy grows.
sentences.zh: 对于我们如何看待这个国家的财富、我们的经济以及我们的经济如何增长，是非常基础的。

sentences.en: You can make the argument that a tax code that favors investment, that doesn't tax wealth, leads to more innovation, more risk-taking.
sentences.zh: 你可以提出这样的论点：一个优待投资、不对财富征税的税法，会带来更多的创新和更多的冒险。

sentences.en: There is enormous reward in our tax code for the risks that Elon Musk have made.
sentences.zh: 我们的税法对埃隆·马斯克所承担的风险给予了巨大的回报。

sentences.en: And, you know, Elon Musk is in the United States for a reason.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，埃隆·马斯克在美国是有原因的。

sentences.en: That's why we have Tesla.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们有特斯拉。

sentences.en: Jeff Bezos created Amazon and the rewards were enormous.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·贝佐斯创造了亚马逊，回报是巨大的。

sentences.en: On the other hand, you could say, look, how much incentive does an Elon Musk need?
sentences.zh: 另一方面，你可以说，看，埃隆·马斯克需要多少激励？

sentences.en: If Jeff Bezos was going to make $100 billion off of Amazon instead of $140 billion, would he have not bothered?
sentences.zh: 如果杰夫·贝佐斯从亚马逊赚到的是1000亿美元而不是1400亿美元，他会不折腾吗？

sentences.en: Would Elon Musk really not have invented Tesla if he had to pay a 2% surtax on some of the wealth gains he does?
sentences.zh: 如果埃隆·马斯克必须对他获得的部分财富收益缴纳2%的附加税，他真的就不会发明特斯拉了吗？

sentences.en: And I think that you could also have to look at what's happening in the broader society.
sentences.zh: 我认为你还必须看看整个社会正在发生什么。

sentences.en: As we see fabulous gains in wealth of the super rich, the vast majority of American workers are pretty stagnant.
sentences.zh: 当我们看到超级富豪的财富获得惊人增长时，绝大多数美国工人的收入却相当停滞。

sentences.en: We are not seeing the kind of class mobility that we once did.
sentences.zh: 我们再也看不到曾经那种阶层流动性了。

sentences.en: The American dream is not as palpable as it once was.
sentences.zh: 美国梦已不再像过去那样触手可及。

sentences.en: And as the gap grows between the very super rich and the middle class, there's a real risk here of political instability, of societal instability.
sentences.zh: 随着超级富豪与中产阶级之间的差距不断扩大，政治和社会动荡的风险真实存在。

sentences.en: And those are the kind of things that policymakers need to look at from right and from the left.
sentences.zh: 这些都是政策制定者无论立场左右都必须审视的问题。

sentences.en: And you know, this ProPublica article has just come out.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，ProPublica 的这篇文章刚刚发布。

sentences.en: We don't know where this is heading.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道事态会如何发展。

sentences.en: We need to watch it.
sentences.zh: 我们需要密切关注。

sentences.en: But honestly, I think we're just at the beginning of this chapter.
sentences.zh: 但老实说，我认为我们才刚刚翻开这一篇章。

sentences.en: Thank you, Jonathan.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，乔纳森。

sentences.en: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是今天你需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: The drugmaker Novavax said that its vaccine against COVID-19 is highly effective in clinical trials, potentially giving Americans a fourth choice for fighting the virus.
sentences.zh: 制药商诺瓦瓦克斯（Novavax）表示，其新冠疫苗在临床试验中表现出极高的有效性，这可能为美国人抗击病毒提供第四种选择。

sentences.en: The company said that the two-dose vaccine offers overall efficacy of 90.4 percent, on par with the vaccines made by Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna,
sentences.zh: 该公司称，这种两剂型疫苗的总体有效率为90.4%，与辉瑞-生物科技（Pfizer-BioNTech）和莫德纳（Moderna）生产的疫苗相当，

sentences.en: and higher than the vaccine made from Johnson & Johnson.
sentences.zh: 且高于强生公司（Johnson & Johnson）生产的疫苗。

sentences.en: But because the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但由于美国

sentences.en: vaccine supply is high, regulators may encourage Novavax to first distribute its doses to other countries where it's more needed.
sentences.zh: 疫苗供应充足，监管机构可能会鼓励诺瓦瓦克斯优先向更需要的国家分发疫苗。

sentences.en: And on Monday, a day after ousting Benjamin Netanyahu as prime minister,
sentences.zh: 周一，在罢免本雅明·内塔尼亚胡总理职务的一天后，

sentences.en: Israel's new government sought to change its image overseas and mend relations with the Biden administration.
sentences.zh: 以色列新政府寻求改变其海外形象，并修复与拜登政府的关系。

sentences.en: In a speech, Foreign Minister Yair Lapid said it had been, quote, reckless and dangerous of Netanyahu to build alliances with Republicans while alienating Democrats, who, he noted,
sentences.zh: 外交部长亚伊尔·拉皮德在演讲中表示，内塔尼亚胡与共和党建立联盟而疏远民主党的做法是“鲁莽且危险的”，他指出，民主党人

sentences.en: now control the U.S.
sentences.zh: 目前

sentences.en: government.
sentences.zh: 掌控着美国政府。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Asta Chaturvedi, Nina Patak, Annie Brown, and Robert Jemison.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由阿斯塔·查图尔维迪、尼娜·帕塔克、安妮·布朗和罗伯特·杰米森制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Paige Cowett and Dave Shaw, engineered by Chris Wood, and contains original music by Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 由佩奇·考维特和戴夫·肖编辑，克里斯·伍德担任工程制作，丹·鲍威尔创作了原创音乐。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，该党就陷入了一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我，莎拉·凯尼格，将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.zh: 请在你获取播客的任何平台收听。
